item.text: {"question_id":"1B.4","answer":"In 2023, China under Xi showed active diplomatic engagement with arms-control and nonproliferation processes: it participated in P5 nuclear-risk discussions, submitted an NPT working paper, held China-US consultations, endorsed the NPT’s three pillars and JCPOA preservation, and called on the largest arsenals to implement New START and make substantial, verifiable, legally binding reductions (BATCH-0015-E007; BATCH-0012-E004; BATCH-0014-E001; BATCH-0025-E018; BATCH-0023-E010). China also called for withdrawal of overseas-deployed nuclear weapons and proposed an intergovernmental safeguards process concerning AUKUS, though these were diplomatic positions rather than demonstrated implementation or inspection outcomes (BATCH-0023-E011; BATCH-0023-E004). The record is materially qualified by China’s 2023 rejection of a fissile-material-production moratorium and by its continuing non-ratification of the CTBT; the latter is an inherited, continuing state status, not evidence of a specific 2023 Xi decision (BATCH-0007-E018; BATCH-0025-E010). The supplied evidence therefore supports genuine but predominantly declaratory and agenda-setting engagement, with no demonstrated treaty ratification, funded implementation, inspection compliance, or concrete Chinese arms reduction during the target period.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E007","BATCH-0012-E004","BATCH-0014-E001","BATCH-0025-E018","BATCH-0023-E010","BATCH-0023-E011"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0007-E018","BATCH-0025-E010","BATCH-0023-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not establish compliance with specific treaty or inspection obligations.","It does not demonstrate funded implementation, concrete Chinese reductions, or measurable outcomes from the diplomatic engagements.","Most evidence is attributed to the Chinese state or delegations rather than to Xi personally.","BATCH-0024-E004 concerns a 2019 position and is background only; it does not establish a 2023 action.","The CTBT non-ratification is current/inherited status, and the supplied record does not identify a 2023 decision or Xi’s reasons for it."],"corrections_made":["Reduced the weight assigned to meetings and working papers by distinguishing diplomatic engagement from agreement implementation or measurable risk reduction.","Added the 2023 calls for verifiable reductions and withdrawal of overseas nuclear weapons.","Added the proposed AUKUS safeguards process as a qualified diplomatic position.","Quarantined CTBT non-ratification as continuing inherited status rather than presenting it as a specific 2023 decision.","Excluded the 2019 trilateral-negotiation position from target-period evidence while retaining it as a limitation on period fit."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":[]}
